text:
Sasha Chen: quick check: new reranker candidate `rdrank-v2-int8` shows NDCG@10 drop ~0.015 vs fp16 baseline on devset, but MRR@10 basically unchanged. anyone seen int8 cause this kind of split? suspect tokenization/padding differences.
Matt R.: can you paste the eval command + seed? also which dev split (dev-full or dev-short)?
Sasha Chen: sure — running eval with this command:```
./eval_rerank.py --model rdrank-v2-int8 \\n  --baseline rdrank-v2-fp16 \\n  --split dev-full \\n  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 \\n  --seed 42 \\n  --normalize-queries True \\n  --pad-docs 512
```seed=42, ran 3 seeds overall.
Priya K: did you quantize with PTQ or QAT? PTQ sometimes shifts embeddings a bit. which backend? :thinking_face:
Sasha Chen: PTQ (post-train) per-channel 8-bit, no bias-correction step. backend is xformers + custom kernels on Dedicated. truncation/padding matches baseline (512). ndcg drop is consistent across seeds 42/101/202. :frowning_face:
Lee: can you paste a couple of queries that flip? short queries often cause ndcg sensitivity.
Sasha Chen: here are two quick examples:```
Query: "How to set up SSO with Okta"
Baseline top doc: "SSO guide (Okta) - setup steps"
Int8 top doc: "Okta troubleshooting and common errors"
// both relevant but ordering changed enough to affect ndcg score
```
Matt R.: did you run pairwise significance / bootstrap? sample size?
Sasha Chen: bootstrap 10k reps (paired), p ~ 0.02 for ndcg@10 (two-sided), MRR p ~ 0.28. so ndcg drop looks borderline significant.
Priya K: two quick things to try: (1) rerun PTQ with bias-correction / per-tensor fallback for softmax, (2) run eval with query/doc normalizer (lowercasing, strip punctuation) to rule out tokenization differences, (3) compute avg cosine similarity between fp16 and int8 query embeddings to quantify drift.
Sasha Chen: good plan — I'll run bias-corrected PTQ and the embedding drift check. also going to add a minimal paired-bootstrapping script to the eval harness. i'll open a small PR with the eval diffs.
